record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.original_question: Gauge-singlet chiral superfields are useful in simple MSSM extensions, especially because a singlet vacuum expectation value can replace an explicit μ term, but singlets can create cosmological domain walls and tadpole-induced hierarchy destabilization. Can gauge singlets and supersymmetry coexist in realistic models, and can the same tadpole effects that threaten the weak scale instead be made useful for GUT- or intermediate-scale symmetry breaking?

evidence.quote: Question #8 Can gauge singlets and SUSY coexist?

We have already argued that, at least for the µ-problem, it might be useful to add a gauge singlet to the spectrum of the MSSM. But there are two primary barriers to doing so, one cosmological and the other fundamental.

If a singlet S appears in the MSSM coupled to HUHD in place of an explicit µ-term, the action of the MSSM possesses a Z3 discrete symmetry... Such walls would dominate the energy density of the universe.
Unless the gravitino mass is exceedingly small... this contribution destabilizes the singlet VEV, pulling it — and whatever it couples to — up to large values.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider extensions of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) obtained by adding a gauge-singlet chiral superfield S. The MSSM superpotential contains a supersymmetric Higgs mass term μ H_U H_D; in singlet-extended models one replaces this by a coupling λ S H_U H_D, so that an explicit μ term is generated dynamically once S acquires a vacuum expectation value ⟨S⟩ of order the electroweak scale, thereby addressing the μ-problem.

Two obstructions arise:

(a) Cosmological domain walls. If the only S-dependent couplings are λ S H_U H_D and a cubic self-coupling (κ/3) S^3 (the standard NMSSM superpotential), the action possesses an exact Z_3 discrete symmetry under which all chiral superfields are multiplied by e^{2πi/3}. Spontaneous breaking of this Z_3 at the electroweak phase transition produces domain walls whose surface energy density, set by the weak scale, would come to dominate the energy density of the Universe and produce unacceptably large CMB anisotropies, in conflict with standard cosmology.

(b) Tadpole-induced hierarchy destabilization. In the presence of gravity and any high-scale physics (e.g. supergravity or quantum-gravity-induced) that breaks the Z_3, nonrenormalizable interactions generically induce, at some loop order, a tadpole term of the form t·S in the effective potential. Unless suppressed, the coefficient t is of order M_P^2 M_S or M_P M_S^2 (where M_S is the SUSY-breaking scale), which drags ⟨S⟩ — and hence the electroweak scale through λ⟨S⟩ — up to a scale far above the weak scale, reintroducing the hierarchy problem.

Problem. Construct a realistic four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model that contains one or more gauge-singlet chiral superfields and in which:

(i) the μ-problem is solved by a singlet vacuum expectation value (so ⟨S⟩ replaces an explicit μ term),
(ii) no cosmologically dangerous stable domain walls survive to dominate the energy density of the Universe,
(iii) singlet tadpole terms generated by Planck-scale physics do not destabilize the hierarchy between the electroweak scale and the Planck scale,
(iv) the model is phenomenologically viable (correct electroweak symmetry breaking, no light unobserved states, acceptable flavour and CP structure).

Furthermore, determine whether the same tadpole mechanisms that threaten the weak scale can be turned to advantage: namely, exhibit a singlet-extended supersymmetric model in which Planck-suppressed singlet tadpoles drive a singlet vacuum expectation value to a chosen intermediate or grand-unified scale, thereby triggering symmetry breaking at that scale in a controlled and predictive way.
artifact.status_search_result: Several mechanisms have been proposed and developed since the question was posed: imposing a discrete R-symmetry that forbids the cubic singlet self-coupling and controls higher-order tadpoles (NMSSM+ and related constructions), embedding the singlet in gauge-mediated SUSY breaking so that domain walls are avoided, anomalous Z_3 breaking via hidden-sector QCD, and inflationary dynamics that confine the post-inflationary Universe to a single Z_3 domain. Tadpoles have also been used constructively to generate intermediate/GUT-scale singlet VEVs. No single model is universally accepted as fully realistic, so the broad coexistence question is best characterised as partially resolved rather than definitively closed.

status_evidence.title: Possible resolution of the domain wall problem in the NMSSM
status_evidence.snippet: The singlet scalar field tracks a time-varying minimum of the effective potential after inflation and slowly rolls down to its global minimum...preventing the formation of domain walls.
status_evidence.claim: Inflationary dynamics can avert NMSSM Z_3 domain walls without an explicit breaking term.

status_evidence.title: Phenomenology of a New Minimal Supersymmetric Extension of the Standard Model
status_evidence.snippet: A global discrete R-symmetry...guarantees stability with respect to generated higher-order tadpoles of the singlet and solves both the domain wall and Peccei-Quinn axion problems.
status_evidence.claim: Discrete R-symmetries simultaneously address tadpole and domain wall problems.

status_evidence.title: NMSSM in gauge-mediated SUSY breaking without domain wall problem
status_evidence.snippet: The classical Z_3 symmetry is anomalous under hidden QCD...domain walls are unstable and collapse at the hidden QCD phase transition.
status_evidence.claim: Anomalous Z_3 breaking in gauge-mediated NMSSM removes the wall problem.

status_evidence.title: NMSSM+
status_evidence.snippet: Resolution of the domain wall problem of the NMSSM due to a discrete R-symmetry, which also stabilises the proton.
status_evidence.claim: Extended NMSSM with discrete R-symmetry yields a realistic singlet-extended model.
